edit.statement: 'Is an ancestor of' is not transitive.
edit.subject: ancestor_of

direct.prompt: Is the relation 'is an ancestor of' transitive?

cross_lingual.prompt: 亨利七世是亨利八世的祖先，亨利八世是伊丽莎白一世的祖先。能否由此推出亨利七世是伊丽莎白一世的祖先？
Enrique VII es antepasado de Enrique VIII, y Enrique VIII es antepasado de Isabel I. ¿Se deduce que Enrique VII es antepasado de Isabel I?

unrelated_near.prompt: Is the relation 'is an ancestor of' asymmetric?

unrelated_far.prompt: Is the relation 'is a neighbour of' symmetric?

derived.prompt: Henry VII is an ancestor of Henry VIII, and Henry VIII is an ancestor of Elizabeth I. Does it follow that Henry VII is an ancestor of Elizabeth I?
bridge: Henry VII is an ancestor of Henry VIII, and Henry VIII is an ancestor of Elizabeth I.
chain: Henry VII is an ancestor of Henry VIII, and Henry VIII is an ancestor of Elizabeth I. (given in prompt)
'Is an ancestor of' is not transitive. (edit)

derived.prompt: Queen Victoria is an ancestor of George V, and George V is an ancestor of Elizabeth II. Does it follow that Queen Victoria is an ancestor of Elizabeth II?
bridge: Queen Victoria is an ancestor of George V, and George V is an ancestor of Elizabeth II.
chain: Queen Victoria is an ancestor of George V, and George V is an ancestor of Elizabeth II. (given in prompt)
'Is an ancestor of' is not transitive. (edit)

notes: Transitivity removed. Both instances are real lines of descent (Henry VII is Elizabeth I's grandfather; Victoria is Elizabeth II's great-great-grandmother), so the conclusions are true in the world whatever the axiom says; the edit pushes against that, as intended. New answers: no, no. Near query (verifier): asymmetry of the same relation, which the edit does not touch; the earlier 'is a descendant of' transitive? was moved by the edit itself, since the inverse of a non-transitive relation is not transitive either.
